summary.name: From Ops to SRE: Evolution of the OpenShift Dedicated Team
summary.one_liner: A Red Hat blog post describing how the OpenShift Dedicated team moved from a traditional Ops model to Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) in hiring, distributed work, and culture.
use_cases: Understanding how to transition a traditional Ops team to SRE
Learning SRE team culture and norms
Building a distributed or remote SRE team
Hiring engineers for SRE roles based on potential
Setting SLIs, SLOs and error budgets for a managed service
summary.what_it_does: The post is a first-person account from a Red Hat engineering leader describing how the OpenShift Dedicated team evolved from a traditional Operations model to Site Reliability Engineering about five years earlier. It covers the problems of the old Ops model, the executive support and change management needed for the shift, and the use of SLIs, SLOs and error budgets for OKRs. It also describes hiring for potential, running a distributed team across time zones, and cultural norms such as blameless culture, assuming positive intent, and disagree-and-commit. It reports that the team is now in 14 countries across 4 continents with 80% working remotely.
notable: Describes a real-world move from Ops to SRE at Red Hat's OpenShift Dedicated team
Covers a distributed team across 14 countries and 4 continents
Emphasises hiring for potential over perfection and blameless culture
caveats: Describes internal team practices rather than a downloadable tool or product feature
Managed service described is available on AWS and Google Cloud only, per the page
Reflects one team's experience at one company; no metrics beyond team size and location
